title: Manifest rule registry
description: The semantic rules a manifest must satisfy, as data. Distinct from extension-manifest.schema.json, which describes the shape: these are the checks a binding runs and the ids it must report, so two bindings can be shown to enforce the same contract rather than merely reaching the same verdict.

blank.description: What counts as blank. Defined here because no two languages' trim functions agree.

id.description: manifest.<field>.<kind>. Namespaced so item rules can be added without renaming.

parameterized.description: True when one manifest can violate this rule more than once — each violation carrying its own JSON Pointer.

supersedes.description: Rules that cannot meaningfully fire once this one has. If a rule fires, none of the rules it supersedes may appear in the same result — stated as a property of the output, so a binding may short-circuit while evaluating or filter afterwards.

enum.description: The permitted values, when the rule is a membership check.

pattern.description: The normative regular expression, in a portable subset: no lookarounds, no backreferences, no Unicode property escapes, and digit classes spelled [0-9] rather than \d, which is ASCII in JavaScript but Unicode-aware in Python and Rust.
